name: @webbula/mcp

tools.name: verify_email
tools.description: Verify exactly ONE email address in real time. Returns a deliverability verdict, any corrected form, and a trust block (data provenance + activity history) so an agent can decide whether the address is safe to use. Use this when the input is a single email address and nothing else. For a list of email addresses use hygiene_check; when the input is a file use upload_file (batch); if the input also includes a name, postal address, or phone, use validate_lead instead.

profile.description: Optional Webbula hygiene profile name. Defaults to the server's configured profile.

tools.name: hygiene_check
tools.description: Run Webbula email hygiene on a LIST of 1..100 email addresses in real time. Returns, per email, its classification, activity history (first/last seen, trajectory), a corrected form when a typo is detected, and a trust block. Use this whenever the input is a list of email addresses (it also works for a single address, though verify_email is the simpler choice there). A list longer than 100 addresses is REJECTED with an error — do not split it or send it to upload_file; the batch flow is for files only. When the input is a file, use upload_file instead; to assess a full contact record with a name, postal address, or phone, use validate_lead instead.

emails.description: The email addresses to check (1..100). A longer list is rejected — use a file with upload_file instead.

profile.description: Optional Webbula hygiene profile name. Defaults to the server's configured profile.

tools.name: get_credits
tools.description: Check the Webbula account's remaining credit BALANCE (not email results) before running a larger job. Returns remaining credits per billing scenario, with an explicit "unlimited" flag for accounts that are not metered. Read-only — it does not verify any email and does not consume verification credits. To verify emails use verify_email / hygiene_check / validate_lead.

tools.name: list_profiles
tools.description: List the Webbula PROFILE NAMES your account is allowed to use (not email results). A profile (or preset) selects the verification/hygiene/lead validations and the billing scenario a call runs under. Use this to discover valid profile names before calling verify_email, hygiene_check, validate_lead, or upload_file, or when one of those rejected a profile — they reject any profile not on this list. Read-only; does not verify emails.

tools.name: validate_lead
tools.description: Validate a full lead/contact record (name, postal address, phone, and/or email) with Webbula's leadHygiene in one real-time call. Assesses any combination supplied — modeled gender, address accuracy and geocode, phone line type — and runs the same email hygiene verdict as verify_email when an email is included. CHOOSE THIS whenever the input has a name, postal address, or phone — even alongside an email; do NOT use verify_email or hygiene_check for records that carry those fields. (For email-only input, use verify_email or hygiene_check.) At least one of first_name, last_name, full_address, phone, or emails is required. Real-time, single tool call.

profile.description: Optional lead-enabled Webbula profile name. Defaults to the server's configured lead profile.

full_address.description: The complete address: street, city, state, and ZIP.

emails.description: Optional email addresses to additionally run hygiene on (max 100).

tools.name: upload_file
tools.description: Submit a FILE of emails for ASYNCHRONOUS batch hygiene. Use this whenever the input is a file (.csv, .txt, .xlsx, .xls) — always route a file here, regardless of how many rows it has. For a list of email addresses passed inline (not a file), use hygiene_check, or verify_email for a single address — a list is never sent to batch. Step 1 of the batch flow: upload_file -> file_status -> download_results. Provide the file inline (base64 + filename) or point at a remote source (web URL, FTP, or SSH). Returns a package_name to poll with file_status and fetch with download_results. Local filesystem paths are not supported.

profile.description: Optional Webbula profile name. Defaults to the server's configured profile.

content_base64.description: Base64-encoded file content (≤ ~1 MiB). Use with `filename`.

filename.description: File name (with a .csv/.txt/.xlsx/.xls extension). Required with `content_base64`.

data_source.description: Remote source type, as an alternative to inline content.

secure.description: Use TLS (SFTP) for the FTP source.

tools.name: file_status
tools.description: Check the status of a batch task (from upload_file) by its package_name. Step 2 of the batch flow: upload_file -> file_status -> download_results. Returns the current stage (preparing → prepared → running → finished → completed, or canceled) with a human-readable label and whether it is terminal, plus — once completed — the list of result files ready to download. Poll this after upload_file until the task is terminal, then call download_results. Only for batch tasks — the real-time tools return results directly and need no polling.

package_name.description: The task handle returned by upload_file.

tools.name: download_results
tools.description: Download a result file from a COMPLETED batch task. Step 3 (final) of the batch flow: upload_file -> file_status -> download_results — only call this once file_status reports the task terminal. Provide the package_name and a filename reported by file_status (e.g. insert.csv for cleaned records, _report.xls for the summary). Returns the file content unchanged — text files as text, binary files base64-encoded.

filename.description: A result filename reported by file_status (e.g. insert.csv, _report.xls).
